data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, the name Santan holds a deep sense of reverence and respect for its-carriers. It is often given to children born in families where the previous generation had produced several offsprings, making the child a part of an ever-expanding family tree. This naming convention reflects the importance of family, continuity and the cyclical nature of life in Hindu culture.

It symbolizes the concept of reincarnation and the continued evolution and growth of the soul through many lifetimes. The name also reminds the bearer of his/her duty to live a virtuous life and contribute positively to the world in order to attain the ultimate goal of moksha or spiritual liberation.
